mechanisms.message: Unsupported operator: matches. Supply an operator override if the database can express it faithfully.
mechanisms.reason: ActiveRecord has no portable RE2 predicate; matches is refused even inside equality or disjunction.

mechanisms.message: Unsupported operator: index. Supply an operator override if the database can express it faithfully.
mechanisms.reason: Relational associations do not expose CEL positional scalar-list indexing; the adapter refuses index before building a query.

mechanisms.message: Unsupported operator: set-field. Supply an operator override if the database can express it faithfully.
mechanisms.reason: The planner emits a struct through set-field; this translator has no structured literal value and refuses that operator.

mechanisms.message: Unsupported operator: except. Supply an operator override if the database can express it faithfully.
mechanisms.reason: The SQL translator has no two-list difference value; the walk refuses except in each arrival position.

Positional access into a scalar list. `index` has no case in the translator's operator dispatch at all, so the walk falls through to the generic unsupported-operator refusal rather than to a leaf-operand guard — which is why the message names the operator and offers an override. No case was written because row order in a SQL relation is not defined without an ORDER BY the plan does not carry: `tagNames` is a has_many association, and `tagNames[0]` names whichever row the engine happens to return first. A caller whose table has a deterministic ordering column can express it faithfully, and the override the message offers is that escape hatch

mechanisms.message: contains requires a string operand, got integer
mechanisms.reason: CEL requires a string for this operation; the mapped ActiveRecord column is numeric or boolean, so SQL coercion would over-grant.

mechanisms.message: add cannot take an operand that may be NaN or Infinity
mechanisms.reason: CEL carries a NaN or a signed Infinity out of the division and through the arithmetic composed on top of it; SQL has no value that does, because the NULLIF divide-by-zero guard turns the whole sum into NULL. The adapter resolves a non-finite division only where the division IS the comparison operand, so a division nested under further arithmetic fails closed instead of emitting the under-granting filter

pins.message: double() needs a numeric column. CEL makes an error for a string that is not a number, and Cerbos denies the row, but SQL gives 0.0 and the filter would keep it. Compare the column directly, or give an operator override.

int() applied to a :string column: CEL reads the WHOLE string or makes an error, and Cerbos then denies the row, but SQL reads the digits at the front and gives a number, so the filter would keep the row. Compare the column directly, or give an operator override.

timestamp() applied to a :string column: this adapter compares instants using the database's own temporal type, so the attribute must map to a datetime column rather than to a column holding a formatted timestamp string
Cannot divide by a column that may be zero

Cannot divide by a column that may be zero: IEEE-754 keeps the sign of a zero, SQL cannot tell -0.0 from 0.0, and thus the sign of the Infinity is unknown. Divide by a constant, or keep this shape out of the policy.
